title: Add consent-based browser recordings and reusable video production
description:
## Summary

- add consent-based local browser action recording, exact recording provenance, and `recordings` status/latest/enable/disable commands
- add `browser-harness video init|review|export` for short explanatory videos made from captured frames
- preserve the established visual style: raw browser frames, cursor-led camera, fast click results, concise subtitles, causal explanation cards, and verified outcome cards
- keep fresh installs off by default while treating natural “record/show/demo” requests as task-level opt-in

## One skill, one feature

Video is now part of browser-harness itself rather than a separately installed skill:

- the main `SKILL.md` owns capture/consent behavior and links one short `interaction-skills/make-video.md` guide
- renderer constants live in code; there is no `openai.yaml`, separate skill package, or editable “house style” JSON
- initialization, compilation, review, and export are normal installed CLI functionality
- the wheel ships the renderer template, so the feature works outside a repository checkout

This revision removed 1,130 lines from the previous version. The PR now has 13 changed files, four of which are the actual new product implementation: recorder, video compiler/CLI, renderer/exporter, and HTML renderer. It adds no test files or test changes.

## Editorial regression guard

The canonical guide now retains the full editing contract from the pre-consolidation skill: causal intent → action → result sequencing, sticky narration that spans 2–3 changing screenshots, authentic captured clicks/cursor/typing, complete evidence coverage, useful Observed → Mistake → Correction detours, semantic routes, and verified outcomes. The compiler rejects mechanical one-caption-per-frame cuts, and accepts up to two pixels of harmless viewport drift so a real click is not discarded for a one-pixel browser resize.

The renderer template is byte-for-byte unchanged from the pre-consolidation implementation, and all pacing/motion constants remain identical.

## Safety and authenticity

- source URLs are dropped at ingest and recording sources are content-hashed
- typed text is private by default; reviewed non-password evidence requires explicit `showTyping`
- selected source/result frames must share a viewport, allowing only two pixels of harmless browser resize drift, so page-coordinate masks cannot drift materially
- export rejects changed evidence, briefs, compositions, renderers, or review artifacts
- captured evidence is never reenacted; post-task recordings require timestamp/page verification
- privacy detection is documented as a backstop, not a guarantee; every used full-resolution frame must be reviewed

## Performance and validation

Cold-agent validation using only the main skill and make-video guide:

- `video init`: passed
- `video review`: 0 errors/warnings
- independent clean agent produced a 16.19s H.264 MP4 with six action frames, two narration cues, all five requested result screens, and the real captured click
- the previously good cut still passes, while the mechanical five-screens/five-captions cut is now rejected
- visual style and normal/reduced-motion sequences preserved
- wheel build includes the CLI modules and renderer template
- skill validation and Python compilation passed

The dominant export cost remains the required real-time canvas capture.

## Release

This PR bumps browser-harness from `0.1.5` to `0.1.6`.


## Live-browser cleanup

Review and export now restore media emulation and the original live-browser attachment before closing their editor tab. Export always restores Chrome’s default download behavior and fails clearly if that restoration cannot be confirmed. `BH_RECORD=0` now refuses explicit recording instead of producing an unusable boundary-only trace. These changes do not touch the renderer, compiler, pacing, camera, or editorial heuristics.

bugs.summary: _start_export always points Chrome download behavior at the recording directory and passes only webm.name, while export() polls for output.with_suffix(".webm") next to the requested --output; for a nested or absolute --output (exports/video.mp4, /elsewhere/video.mp4) the webm lands in the recording directory, the poll never sees it and the export times out (and a nested output directory is never created).
bugs.trigger: Run browser-harness video export with --output exports/video.mp4 (or an absolute path outside the recording directory) after a successful review.
